title: Checkout requests intermittently fail with HTTP 504 timeouts
description: From 16 August 2026 14:05 UTC to 14:42 UTC, the ShopFlow checkout service experienced intermittent failures during order placement. Customers reported that checkout requests were taking 10-30 seconds and eventually returning HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout errors. Existing orders were also taking longer than normal to complete. Product browsing and shopping-cart functionality remained operational. The issue was concentrated in checkout-service.

evidence.content: The checkout-service stores orders in PostgreSQL. Relationship: orders.customer_id -> customers.id. Checkout queries frequently filter or join using orders.customer_id. The orders table contains several million records. Indexes on frequently queried foreign-key columns are important for preventing expensive sequential scans.

Long-running database queries can hold connections for extended periods. When enough connections remain occupied: Long queries -> connections remain busy -> pool utilization increases -> connection acquisition waits -> requests timeout. Connection pool exhaustion can therefore be a consequence of expensive database queries rather than the original root cause.
Normal Checkout Baseline: Checkout query latency <200ms, Database connection utilization <70%, HTTP 504 rate <0.1%, PostgreSQL CPU <70%.
